evidence_level: L2 (real firmware + 6DOF plant + sensor models, SIL only)
source_state: scalar Eigen SIL; descent target starts at current altitude; ground reset locks target to current altitude

metrics.landed: final_alt < 1.0 m at end of run
metrics.land_t: first time truth altitude < 0.5 m after exceeding 1.0 m
metrics.land_hold: horizontal displacement from hold target at first touchdown
metrics.land_vz_down: truth vertical speed at first touchdown, NED down positive
metrics.max_desc_vz_down: maximum truth vertical speed before touchdown
metrics.max_roll_preland: maximum absolute roll before first touchdown

caveats: The 60 s cells reproduce the 20 s cells exactly: the emergency descent reaches the ground by 33.6-39.7 s, before either outage ends. They are not independent long-outage tests and are excluded from the figure.

The SIL starts on the ground and climbs at ~0.9-1.0 m/s. At the 20 s outage start the vehicle is at ~8 m; at the 26 s descent trigger it is at ~14.6 m. The --alt value is a target altitude, not the actual altitude. After the target-origin fix, 20 m and 30 m target cells are behaviorally identical.

Pre-fix stale-target runs were discarded: the ramp started from the takeoff target (30 m), so when the vehicle touched down early and GNSS recovered, the residual target pulled it back up (r1: 15/120 climbed to 12-16 m; r2: 33/120 hovered at 1-3.7 m). Fix: ramp starts at current altitude; on ground + GNSS recovery target is locked to current altitude.
Touchdown speed is measured against the plant ground constraint; there is no landing gear, impact absorption, or ground friction model. Values are kinematic impact speeds, not structural limits.

During the GNSS outage the EKF vertical velocity lags the truth by up to ~5 m/s (trace seed1: truth -4.11 m/s, EKF +0.68 m/s at t=40 s). A 20-seed A/B using a 0.5 s baro-altitude slope for the descent inner loop made the 1 m/s case worse (median touchdown 3.53 vs 1.25 m/s) and did not improve 2/3 m/s; that variant was rejected and its results are archived separately.
All numbers are scalar-Eigen SIL L2, not real aircraft.

A ground-dwell latch (target=current altitude after 1 s below 0.3 m) was added after these runs. It changes only post-touchdown target/throttle behavior; land_t/land_hold/land_vz_down/max_roll_preland are measured before it applies and are unaffected.
